The OTEC hull column passes through the splash zone by necessity to allow for personnel access from the platform topsides. The cylindrical shape helps to resist storm forces; however, additional external supports may be warranted in the wave crashing zone. The additional weight introduced by potential external supports will need to be accounted for in the overall design. The small equipment such as refrigerant pumps, turbine generator, electrical equipment, instrumentation, and associated piping components can be maintained within the add-on hull column and their replacement can be accomplished using the platform crane via a hatch on the top of the add-on hull column. The larger equipment, including the WW pump, CW pump, condenser, and evaporator will be more challenging to maintain and replace as they are located outside the middle add-on hull column and inside the protective shroud. Replacement of a pump or heat exchanger, although infrequent, will require underwater work involving divers and sophisticated underwater tools, as well as detailed planning and job safety analysis. 4.2.2.2 Maximum (3.9 MW) Add-On Configuration In contrast with the Medium (1 MW) configuration, the key difference making the Maximum (3.9 MW) configuration stand out is the use of the maximum available cold-water intake pipe. The pipe diameter of 3.25 m (the largest size currently commercially available) allows for sufficient cold-water intake to maximize power production. The maximum power production is accommodated by increasing the number of condensers and evaporators to 4 of each. Because this arrangement is more complex, unlike the medium (1 MW) case, all the equipment for the maximum plant is enclosed in a compartmentalized enclosure, providing maximum protection from storms and minor collision risks. Furthermore, the enclosure is comprised of several parts: (1) the main hull, which houses the key components of the OTEC system, such as the evaporators, condensers, the ammonia circulation system, ballast tanks and seawater pumping; (2) the middle hull, which contains the turbine generators and other auxiliary equipment; and (3) the center column, which spans the entire height of the main and middle hulls, and extends all the way up to the working deck on the host platform.
